newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aegon 9-month profit seen rising 16.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Aegon 9-month profit seen rising 16.2 pct.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon NV is expected to surpass its first-half 1996 growth rate with analysts forecasting an increase of 16.2 percent in earnings over the first nine months of 1996.

Twelve analysts polled by Reuters said the Dutch life insurer would on November 15 announce profits between 1,050 and 1,148 million guilders compared to 943 million guilders in the same period of 1995.
During the first six months of 1996, profits increased by 15.7 percent to 711 million guilders.
The consensus on Aegon's nine month profit was nearly 1,096 million guilders, up 16.2 percent.

"Earnings in the first nine months show an even higher increase than during the first half of 1996, with growth in the life insurance sector in its home market of the Netherlands carrying through, better results in non-life and a strong contribution from its British unit Scottish Equitable," said analyst Tom Muller of NIBStrating.
Aegon raised its stake in Scottish Equitable from 60 to 80 percent on January 1 and will increase it gradually to 100 percent by the end of 1998.
Analysts Nico van Geest of Suez and Jean-Paul van Bavel of Van Lanschot Bankiers did not expect any surprises, saying Aegon's future profits were secure as long as life premiums increased.
The life sector, from which stems 81 percent of Aegon's earnings, is likely to increase to 85 percent, analysts said.
Analysts said Aegon should be on the lookout for new acquisitions.
"They did not fulfil any takeovers for quite some time," said Van Bavel, adding the next big acquisition could be in the United States.
"Competition in the U.S. is becoming more fierce," said Muller of NIBStrating, adding firms were working on a larger scale. "As a leading financial firm, Aegon should expand," said Muller.
About one third of Aegon's group income stems from the U.S.
Last week, Aegon chairman Kees Storm said it had put aside about two billion guilders for new acquisitions.
Analysts said prices in the U.S. for acquisitions were even higher than in Europe.
-- Wendy Braanker, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000 ($ = 1.686 Dutch Guilders)
